# OPENING: Jesus Christ had no biological father

**Position.** By "biological father" I mean the man whose seed begets the child. I hold that the KJV gives Jesus Christ a mother, Mary, and names the Holy Ghost, not a man, as the source of his conception. Joseph is his reckoned father in the household and in the genealogy, and he is not the begetter. [L4] Each step below is footed on at least two lower layers.

---

## 1. The genealogy breaks its own pattern at the last link

[L1] Matthew 1:2: "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob; and Jacob begat Judas and his brethren."

[L1] Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."

[L2] In Matthew 1:2 the verb is *egennēsen* (G1080, gennaō, "begat", active voice, the man as agent). In Matthew 1:16 the last verb is *egennēthē* (the same root, passive voice, "was born"). The relative pronoun *hēs* ("of whom") is feminine singular, so it points back to Mary and not to Joseph. Joseph is called *anēr* (G435, "husband"), not the one who begat.

[L3] Matthew 1:20 supports this. The angel calls Joseph "thou son of David" and tells him to "take unto thee Mary thy wife". The command is to take her (*paralabein*, "to take to oneself"). It is not a command to acknowledge a child he had begotten.

[L4] The chain: the active "begat" runs through every earlier link (L1, Matthew 1:2). In the last link the verb turns passive and the relative pronoun turns feminine (L1 Matthew 1:16, L2 *egennēthē* and *hēs*). So the text itself carries the line of begetting to Joseph and then passes to Mary as the one of whom Jesus was born.

## 2. Mary was a virgin when she conceived

[L1] Luke 1:27: "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David; and the virgin's name was Mary."

[L2] *Parthenos* (G3933) means "virgin".

[L1] Luke 1:34: "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"

[L2] *Ginōskō* (G1097, "to know") is the verb of sexual knowledge.

[L3] Genesis 4:1: "And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain". Here "knew" is followed by conception, so Mary's "I know not a man" states that no conception by a man has taken place.

[L1] Matthew 1:23: "Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel, which being interpreted is, God with us."

[L1] Isaiah 7:14: "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel."

[L2] The Hebrew word behind "virgin" in Isaiah 7:14 is *ʿalmāh* (H5959). [L3] Genesis 24:16 says of Rebekah: "a virgin, neither had any man known her". Genesis 24:43 then uses the same *ʿalmāh* of her: "when the virgin cometh forth to draw water". So the KJV uses this word for a woman no man has known.

[L4] Matthew 1:22 says "all this was done, that it might be fulfilled which was spoken of the Lord by the prophet", and then quotes Isaiah 7:14. Luke 1:27 and Luke 1:34 show Mary as a virgin who has not known a man. The conception that follows is therefore not a conception by a man.

## 3. The stated source of the conception is the Holy Ghost

[L1] Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."

[L2] "Of" is *ek* (G1537, "out of", the source). The phrase is *ek pneumatos hagiou*, "out of Holy Spirit".

[L1] Matthew 1:20: "for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."

[L2] "Conceived" is *gennēthen* (from G1080, "begotten"). The verse says that what has been begotten in her is *ek pneumatos hagiou* ("out of the Holy Spirit"). The word for begetting is the one Matthew 1:2 uses for a man's begetting, and here the source of it is the Holy Ghost.

[L1] Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."

[L2] *Dio* ("for which cause") ties the title "Son of God" to the Holy Ghost's coming. *Ek sou* ("out of thee") names Mary as the one from whom he is born.

[L3] Luke 1:31: "thou shalt conceive in thy womb". Hebrews 10:5: "a body hast thou prepared me". Both agree that the body of Jesus is prepared and conceived in the mother.

[L4] Matthew 1:20 gives the begetting-word (L2) with its source (L1, "of the Holy Ghost"). Luke 1:35 gives the cause (L2 *dio*, "for which cause") and the instrument (L1, "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee"). The Holy Ghost is stated as the source, and no man is named in that place.

## 4. Joseph is father by reckoning, not by begetting

[L1] Luke 3:23: "And Jesus himself began to be about thirty years of age, being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph".

[L2] *Enomizeto* (G3543, "was reckoned, was supposed") is the word behind "as was supposed". It marks a reckoning by others and does not state a begetting.

[L1] Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son: and he called his name JESUS."

[L2] *Ginōskō* ("to know") is again the sexual verb. [L3] Matthew 1:20 and Matthew 1:18 supply the sequence. She was found with child "before they came together" (Matthew 1:18), and Joseph did not know her until she had brought forth.

[L1] Luke 2:48: "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing."

[L1] Luke 2:49: "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?"

[L2] *Patēr* (G3962, "father") covers the man who raises and the man who begets. In Luke 2:49 Jesus answers Mary's "thy father" with "my Father's business" (*en tois tou patros mou*, "in the things of my Father"). He points to a different Father than the one Mary named.

[L3] Matthew 1:19 shows Joseph's conduct before the angel speaks: "Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily". Matthew 1:20 then has the angel give the reason for taking her: what is conceived in her "is of the Holy Ghost".

[L4] Luke 3:23 says his fatherhood by Joseph was "supposed" (L1, L2 *enomizeto*). Matthew 1:25 says Joseph did not know Mary until the birth (L1, L2 *ginōskō*, L3 Genesis 4:1). Luke 2:48–49 sets Mary's "thy father" beside Jesus's "my Father's business" (L1, L3). The word "father" in Luke 2:48 therefore names Joseph's place in the household and does not name the begetter.

## 5. The conclusion

[L4] Matthew 1:16 turns from "begat" to "of whom was born" (§1). Mary is a virgin who has not known a man (§2). The begetting is "of the Holy Ghost" (§3). Joseph's fatherhood is "as was supposed" (§4). Together these four steps support the answer that Jesus Christ had no human biological father.

# CHALLENGE: Christ had a biological father, and the text names him Joseph

**Position.** I agree with the defender's definition: the biological father is "the man whose seed begets the child." I hold that the text names that man: Joseph, "of the house and lineage of David" (Luke 2:4). The child is "made of the seed of David according to the flesh" (Romans 1:3). "Of the Holy Ghost" names the covenant origin and the anointing power. It does not name the begetter of the flesh. I hold every row the defender quoted as it is written. I show below how each fits this chain, and I aim at the keystone, LINK D5.

---

## MY CHAIN

[L1] 2 Samuel 7:12: "I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels, and I will establish his kingdom." David's own body is the source.

[L1] Acts 2:30: "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne". Peter names David's loins as the source of Christ's flesh.

[L2] "Loins" is *osphys* (G3751), "the loin; by extension procreative power." It is the same word as Hebrews 7:10: "For he was yet in the loins of his father". That verse also uses *patēr* (G3962, "father"). The loins are a father's.

[L1] Romans 1:3: "which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh". [L2] *ek spermatos* means "out of seed" (*sperma*, G4690, "seed"). *kata sarka* means "according to the flesh."

[L3] Psalm 132:11: "Of the fruit of thy body will I set upon thy throne. [body: Heb. belly]". Hebrews 7:14: "For [it is] evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda". Numbers 1:18: "they declared their pedigrees after their families, by the house of their fathers". [L2] Numbers 1:18 reads *le-veit avotam*: *bayith* (H1004, "house") and *'ab* (H1, "father").

[L4] The promise names David's bowels, loins and body as the source (L1 2 Samuel 7:12, Acts 2:30). *osphys* is a father's procreative power and *sperma* is seed according to the flesh (L2). A tribe is made "evident" by pedigree "by the house of their fathers" (L3 Hebrews 7:14, Numbers 1:18). So the flesh of Christ came down a father's line out of a man's loins.

**C2. The text names that father in the mouths of the mother, the narrator, the town, a disciple and the angel.**

[L1] Luke 2:48: "his mother said unto him, Son, why hast thou thus dealt with us? behold, thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing." [L2] *ho patēr sou* means "thy father." These are Mary's own words.

[L3] Luke 2:33: "Joseph and his mother marvelled at those things which were spoken of him." Luke 2:41: "his parents went to Jerusalem every year". John 6:42: "Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know?" John 1:45: "Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph." Matthew 1:20: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost. [conceived: Gr. begotten]".

[L4] Mary names Joseph "thy father" (L1, L2 *patēr*). Luke's narration pairs "Joseph and his mother" as "his parents," and the town and a disciple say "the son of Joseph" (L3). The one man named beside the mother, in every register, is Joseph of David's house.

**C3. "Of the Holy Ghost," "come upon," "overshadow" and "Son of God" are covenant and empowerment words.**

It is also the verb of Acts 5:15: "the shadow of Peter passing by might overshadow some of them. [into...: or, in every street]". At those rows the verbs name power and presence upon the apostles, the disciples and the sick.

[L3] The title "Son of God" is given in Luke 1:32, before Mary's question: "He shall be great, and shall be called the Son of the Highest: and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David". The flesh is "of the seed of David" (C1).

**C4 (my keystone). Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal, and the child is of his loins.**

[L1] Genesis 4:1: "And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived". This is the stated means of begetting.

[L1] Matthew 1:19: "Joseph her husband". Matthew 1:20: "Mary thy wife". [L3] Deuteronomy 22:24 calls a betrothed damsel "his neighbour's wife."

[L1] Matthew 1:24-25: "took unto him his wife: And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son". [L2] *heōs hou* means "till." It bounds the abstaining from the taking (1:24) to the birth.

[L4] The seed must come out of a man's loins (C1). Begetting is by knowing (L1 Genesis 4:1). Joseph and Mary are husband and wife from the espousal (L1 Matthew 1:19-20, L3 Deuteronomy 22:24). The "till" bounds the abstinence to the pregnancy after the taking (L2 *heōs hou*). So Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal, and the child is "of the seed of David according to the flesh."

"Of the Holy Ghost" and "Son of God" stand in that same record as the covenant origin and title. [L4, footed on C1 to C4 below]

---

## MY CHAIN

**C1. The promised seed comes out of a man's body.**

- [L1] 2 Samuel 7:12: "I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels."
- [L1] Acts 2:30: "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne."
- [L1] Romans 1:3: "which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh."
- [L2] *zera'* (H2233, "seed, posterity") stands in 2 Samuel 7:12. *osphys* (G3751, "the loin, procreative power") stands in Acts 2:30. *spermatos* (G4690, "seed") stands in Romans 1:3, joined to *kata sarka* ("according to the flesh").
- [L3] Hebrews 7:10: "For he was yet in the loins of his father, when Melchisedec met him." Hebrews 7:5 uses the same loins-word for descent: "though they come out of the loins of Abraham."
- [L4] The promise says seed, bowels and loins, and adds "according to the flesh." Hebrews 7:10 places seed in "the loins of his father." So the flesh of Christ is seed carried down a father's loins from David.

**C2. Descent is evident by the house of the fathers.**

- [L1] Hebrews 7:14: "evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda."
- [L3] Numbers 1:18: "they declared their pedigrees after their families, by the house of their fathers."
- [L3] Luke 2:4 gives the one man so placed: "(because he was of the house and lineage of David:)" and that man is Joseph.
- [L2] *bayith* (H1004, "house, family") and *'ab* (H1, "father") stand in Numbers 1:18.
- [L4] Hebrews calls Judah's descent "evident." The law declares pedigree by the fathers' house. Luke 2:4 places Joseph in David's house. So the evident line runs through Joseph.

**C3. The father is named in every register.**

- Mary: [L1] Luke 2:48: "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing."
- The narrator: [L1] Luke 2:33: "Joseph and his mother marvelled," and Luke 2:41: "his parents went to Jerusalem every year."
- A disciple: [L1] John 1:45: "Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph."
- The town: [L1] John 6:42: "the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know."
- The angel: [L1] Matthew 1:20: "Joseph, thou son of David."
- [L2] *patēr* (G3962, "father") stands in Luke 2:48. *goneis* ("parents") stands in Luke 2:41.

**C4. "Of the Holy Ghost" and "Son of God" are the covenant origin and title, given beside a father.**

- [L1] 1 Chronicles 28:6: "Solomon thy son ... I have chosen him to be my son, and I will be his father." In one verse Solomon has David as his father and the LORD's title of son.
- [L1] Psalm 2:7: "Thou art my Son; this day have I begotten thee." [margin: the decree: or, for a decree]
  - [L3] Its three New Testament occasions are these:
    - Acts 13:33: "he hath raised up Jesus again; as it is also written in the second psalm, Thou art my Son, this day have I begotten thee."
    - Hebrews 5:5: "Thou art my Son, to day have I begotten thee," said of the priesthood.
    - Hebrews 1:5: "Thou art my Son, this day have I begotten thee? And again, I will be to him a Father, and he shall be to me a Son?"
- [L3] Romans 1:4: "declared to be the Son of God with power ... by the resurrection from the dead." [margin: declared: Gr. determined]
- [L2] *gennaō* (G1080, "beget") with *ek* (G1537, "out of") God is said of believers. 1 John 5:1 reads: "every one that loveth him that begat loveth him also that is begotten of him." [margin: is born: Gr. has been born]
- [L4] The begetting-word with God as source is used at the resurrection and of believers. Solomon carries the son-title while David is his father. So "of the Holy Ghost" and "Son of God" stand beside a human father in the text's own pattern.

**C5. Keystone.**

- [L1] Genesis 4:1: "Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived." [margin: Cain: that is, Gotten, or, Acquired]
- [L1] Matthew 1:19: "Joseph her husband."
- [L1] Matthew 1:20: "Mary thy wife."
- [L3] Deuteronomy 22:24: "because he hath humbled his neighbour's wife." The law calls the betrothed damsel a wife.
- [L1] Matthew 1:25: "knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son." "Till" bounds the abstinence to the pregnancy.
- [L4, on C1 to C4 and these rows] Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal. The child is of his loins, "of the seed of David according to the flesh." Christ had a biological father, Joseph.

# Round 2: the defender answers

## A. The question put to me: how is it "evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda"?

[L1] Hebrews 7:14: "For [it is] evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda; of which tribe Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood."

I give two rows. Neither needs Joseph as begetter.

**Row 1: the flesh of David's seed is carried out of the woman.**
- [L1] Romans 1:3: "which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh."
- [L1] Galatians 4:4: "God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law."
- [L2] Both verses carry the same participle, *genomenou / genomenon*, from *ginomai* (G1096, "to become, to be made, to come into being"). In both the source is marked by *ek* (G1537, "out of"): *ek spermatos Dabid* ("out of the seed of David") and *ek gynaikos* ("out of a woman").
- [L3] Matthew 1:16 gives the same shape: "of whom was born Jesus."
- [L4] One participle and one preposition govern both the woman and David's seed. The Son is "made" out of David's seed in Romans 1:3 and "made" out of a woman in Galatians 4:4. So the seed of David is the seed that comes out of her. This stands on the shared [L2] construction and the two [L1] verses, and it does not need the genealogy of Joseph.

**Row 2: the house of the fathers reckons the child to Joseph by law.**
- [L3] Numbers 1:18: "they declared their pedigrees after their families, by the house of their fathers."
- [L2] *bayith* (H1004, "house, family") stands in Numbers 1:18. It names a household, not only a begetting.
- [L1] Matthew 1:20: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife."
- [L1] Matthew 1:25: "and he called his name JESUS."
- [L3] Genesis 48:5: "are mine; as Reuben and Simeon, they shall be mine." Sons not begotten by Jacob are reckoned by the father's naming.
- [L3] Ruth 4:17: "There is a son born to Naomi." Ruth bore him, and the house reckons him to Naomi.
- [L4] Joseph is told to take the wife and he names the child. The text's own pattern in Genesis 48:5 and Ruth 4:17 reckons a child to a house by acknowledgment. So Hebrews 7:14's "evident" rests on the legal house through Joseph (Luke 2:4) and on the seed through the woman (Row 1). Acts 2:30's "fruit of his loins" is lineage language. Hebrews 7:10 puts Levi "in the loins of his father" Abraham with Isaac and Jacob between, and Hebrews 7:5 says "they come out of the loins of Abraham". The loins-idiom therefore names descent from an ancestor, not the immediate begetter.

**Row 3: Joseph's own line carries a bar.** [L4, three rows]
- [L1] Matthew 1:11: "Josias begat Jechonias."
- [L1] Matthew 1:16: "Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary."
- [L1] Jeremiah 22:30: "no man of his seed shall prosper, sitting upon the throne of David."
- [L1] Luke 1:32: "the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David."
- [L2] *zera'* (H2233, "seed, posterity") is the word in the earlier pattern of 2 Samuel 7:12.
- [L4] Joseph is of Jechonias's descent (Matthew 1:11–12, 1:16). Jeremiah 22:30 bars any "of his seed" from David's throne, and Luke 1:32 gives the child that throne. So the throne's heir is not the seed of Joseph. It follows that the child is Joseph's by legal house (Row 2) and not by seed.

## B. Answers to the presses

### Against D1 (Matthew 1:18, 1:20)

- [L1] Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son."
- [L2] *heōs* (G2193, "until") bounds the not-knowing at the birth. *ginōskō* (G1097, "to know") is the verb of Luke 1:34, "I know not a man".
- [L1] Matthew 1:18: "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
- The challenger says "came together" (G4905) is her entering his house, and cites Matthew 1:24: "took unto him his wife".
- [L4] Grant that reading. Matthew 1:24 is the taking, and Matthew 1:25 follows it with "knew her not till she had brought forth." So the knowing does not occur before the taking (1:18), and it does not occur after the taking until the birth (1:25). No span between conception and birth is left in which Joseph "knew" her. This answers C5's keystone, "Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal." Matthew 1:25 states the opposite.
- The pattern in Genesis 4:1 and 4:25 runs the other way.
  - [L1] Genesis 4:1: "Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived."
  - [L1] Genesis 4:25: "Adam knew his wife again; and she bare a son."
  - [L2] *yāda'* (H3045, "to know") is the verb in both.
  - [L4] In Genesis the knowing is stated and the conceiving follows. In Matthew 1:25 the knowing is negated up to the birth. The row the challenger brings as pattern shows what Matthew 1:25 denies.
- Press on the *gar* ("for") of Matthew 1:20, which gives the husband and the son of David in the same breath:
  - [L1] Matthew 1:19: "Joseph her husband, being a just [man]... was minded to put her away privily."
  - [L1] Matthew 1:20: "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."
  - [L2] *phobeō* (G5399, "to be alarmed, to be afraid") is the verb of the command "fear not".
  - [L4] Joseph's alarm in 1:19 is that he must put away a wife found with child. The ground the angel gives is that the conception is "of the Holy Ghost" (*ek pneumatos hagiou*, "out of the Holy Ghost"). That ground removes the alarm only if the child's origin was other than Joseph's. A word that named Joseph as source would give no ground for removing it.
- Press from 1 John 5:1 and 4:7, "begotten of him", "born of God":
  - I grant that the same *gennaō* with *ek* God is said of believers who have human fathers.
  - [L1] Matthew 1:20: "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."
  - [L2] The verb is *gennaō* (G1080, "to beget, to bear, to conceive"). Its object is "that which is conceived in her", and the *ek* marks the source of the thing in her womb.
  - [L3] 1 John 5:1 says believers are begotten of God when they believe, as a new birth.
  - [L4] The believer's begetting of God is spoken of a man already born. Matthew 1:20 is spoken of the conception in the womb, with Matthew 1:18 and 1:25 setting no man's knowing beside it. The two rows speak of different objects.

### Against D2 (Luke 1:34–35)

- [L1] Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."
- [L2] *dio kai* ("for which reason also") follows the clauses of verse 35 itself, so its antecedent is the Holy Ghost's coming and the Highest's overshadowing. It looks back to the title of 1:32 only as to the title that 1:35 now grounds.
- [L1] Luke 1:34: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"
- [L2] *epei* ("seeing, since") makes her not-knowing a man the ground of her question *pōs estai touto* ("how shall this be").
- [L4] The question asks how a conception shall come to one who knows no man. The reply names a cause, the Holy Ghost and the power of the Highest, and the title follows from that cause. The reply to a woman who knows no man is not "thou shalt know thy husband".
- Press from Acts 1:8 ("is come upon you") and Luke 9:34 ("there came a cloud, and overshadowed them"):
  - [L2] Both verbs, *eperchomai* (G1904, "to come upon") and *episkiazō* (G1982, "to overshadow"), have the Holy Ghost or a cloud of God's presence as the agent and no man as agent. Acts 1:8 and Luke 9:34 stand as the challenger gave them.
  - [L4] In the rows pressed the agent is divine. That fits Luke 1:35, whose agent is the Holy Ghost, and it does not turn the angel's words toward Joseph.
- Press from tense:
  - [L1] Luke 1:31: "thou shalt conceive in thy womb."
  - [L4] Her present "I know not a man" (Luke 1:34) is joined to a future conception (1:31). The reply of 1:35 supplies the cause for that future conception, a cause that is not a man's. Matthew 1:25's "knew her not till she had brought forth" carries her state through the whole pregnancy.

### Against D3 (Matthew 1:16)

- I grant that "born of women" (Matthew 11:11) and "born of a woman" (Job 14:1) are said of men with fathers.
- My link does not rest on that phrase alone. It rests on the break in the verb pattern.
  - [L1] Matthew 1:2: "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob."
  - [L1] Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus."
  - [L2] *egennēsen* (G1080, active, "begat") is the verb of each earlier link. In 1:16 the verb for Jesus is *egennēthē* (G1080, passive, "was born"), and the relative *hēs* ("of whom") is feminine, naming Mary.
  - [L4] The line runs "A begat B" up to Joseph. At Joseph the construction becomes "the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus." The challenger's rows in Genesis 4:25 and Luke 1:13 give "bare" alongside a named father, and in those verses the father's name stands in a clause that says he knew or has the son. Matthew 1:16 names Joseph as begetter of no one except the child's mother's husband. Matthew 1:25 supplies the stated reason.

### Against D4 (Isaiah 7:14)

- [L1] Genesis 24:43: "when the virgin cometh forth to draw [water]."
- [L1] Genesis 24:16: "the damsel [was] very fair to look upon, a virgin, neither had any man known her: and she went down to the well."
- [L2] Genesis 24:43 uses *'almah* (H5959). Genesis 24:16 uses *bethulah* (H1330, "virgin").
- I grant that the two verses carry different Hebrew words. My point is the person. The "virgin" who comes forth to draw in 24:43 is the damsel who "went down to the well" in 24:16.
- [L4] The *'almah* of 24:43 is Rebekah, and 24:16 states of Rebekah that "neither had any man known her." So the KJV uses *'almah* of a woman whom no man had known. The Proverbs 30:19 "maid" and Exodus 2:8 "maid" are different persons. That the word may elsewhere be rendered "maid" does not remove 24:43.
- [L1] Isaiah 7:14: "Therefore the Lord himself shall give you a sign."
- [L2] *'ôwth* (H226, "sign, token") is the word for the sign. Isaiah 8:3 ("I went unto the prophetess; and she conceived") is not the sign of 7:14: it gives the child another name, Mahershalalhashbaz, while 7:14 gives Immanuel.
- [L1] Matthew 1:22–23: "Now all this was done, that it might be fulfilled... Behold, a virgin shall be with child."
- [L2] Matthew's word is *parthenos* (G3933, "virgin").
- [L4] A sign given by the Lord himself is joined in Matthew 1:22 to "all this", which includes Matthew 1:18 (found with child "before they came together") and 1:25. An espoused virgin (Luke 1:27) is still a virgin. The two rows of Luke 1:27 and Luke 1:34 stand together without strain.

### Against D5 (Luke 3:23; Mary and David)

**Discipline on a link.** Luke 1:27 does not by itself state that Mary is "of the house of David", since the phrase sits after "a man whose name was Joseph". I do not rest Mary's descent on that clause. I rest it on the footing of Section A, Row 1 (Romans 1:3 with Galatians 4:4). Luke 1:36 names Elisabeth as Mary's "cousin" and does not decide the point either way.

- [L1] Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph."
- [L2] *enomizeto* (G3543, from *nomizō*, "to reckon, to hold by custom, to suppose") is the word. In Acts 16:13 "where prayer was wont to be made" gives what was held by custom. In Luke 3:23 the KJV itself renders it "as was supposed".
- [L4] The narrator of Luke 3:23 puts "as was supposed" before Joseph's sonship and gives the next links ("which was [the son] of Heli") with no such qualifier. Luke 3:23 qualifies Joseph's sonship alone.
- [L1] Luke 2:48: "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing."
- [L1] Luke 2:49: "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?"
- [L3] 1 Chronicles 28:6, "Solomon thy son... I will be his father", gives David as father by 2 Samuel 7:12 ("out of thy bowels") with a covenant fatherhood beside it. For Christ, the covenant fatherhood of Luke 2:49 is not set beside a stated begetting by Joseph. What is stated is Luke 1:35, Matthew 1:18 and Matthew 1:25.
- [L1] John 6:42: "Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know? how is it then that he saith, I came down from heaven?"
- [L4] Mary's "thy father" (Luke 2:48) is household speech. The town's "we know" in John 6:42 is answered in the same verse by the child's claim, "I came down from heaven". The narrator who writes "his parents" in Luke 2:41 is the narrator who wrote "as was supposed" in Luke 3:23.

## C. Where the chain stands

1. [L1] Matthew 1:18, 1:20, 1:25: found with child "before they came together"; "knew her not till she had brought forth".
2. [L1] Luke 1:34–35: "I know not a man" is answered with the Holy Ghost and the power of the Highest.
3. [L1] Matthew 1:16: the verb changes from *egennēsen* to *egennēthē*, and "of whom" is feminine.
4. [L1] Matthew 1:22–23 with Isaiah 7:14 and Genesis 24:16, 24:43: the sign is a virgin's conception.
5. [L1] Luke 3:23 "as was supposed", with Romans 1:3 and Galatians 4:4: Joseph is father by reckoning of the house, and David's seed is made out of the woman.
6. [L4] On links 1 to 5 and the Jeremiah 22:30 row: Christ had no biological human father. The conception was "of the Holy Ghost", and Joseph was the legal and supposed father only.

# OPENING: Christ had no human biological father

**Position.** The standard reading is that Christ was conceived in Mary by the Holy Ghost, with no human father. Joseph was husband and legal guardian, and the people only supposed him to be the father. I argue this from the 1611 KJV alone.

## I. Matthew's genealogy stops begetting at Joseph

**[L1] Matthew 1:2:** "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob; and Jacob begat Judas and his brethren."

**[L1] Matthew 1:16:** "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."

**[L2]** The verb behind "begat" is ἐγέννησεν (egennēsen, "begat, fathered"). It runs through the whole list. In verse 16 it is not used of Joseph and Jesus. The text names Joseph as "the husband" (ἀνήρ, anēr, "husband, man") of Mary. The relative pronoun in "of whom" is ἐξ ἧς (ex hēs, "out of whom"), and it is feminine singular. It points to Mary alone, not to Joseph.

**[L4]** Matthew 1:2 sets the pattern "X begat Y", and Matthew 1:16 deliberately breaks it. The "begat" chain runs to Joseph and ends. Jesus is "born" out of the feminine "whom". The break is the evangelist's own marking of who did and did not beget.

---

## II. The stated source of the conception is the Holy Ghost, not a man

**[L1] Matthew 1:18:** "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."

**[L1] Matthew 1:20:** "…fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."

**[L2]** "Of the Holy Ghost" is ἐκ πνεύματος ἁγίου (ek pneumatos hagiou, "out of the Holy Spirit"). The preposition ἐκ (ek, "out of, from") marks the origin. The text says what is conceived in her comes out of the Holy Ghost.

**[L3] Luke 1:35:** "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."

**[L2]** "Of thee" is ἐκ σοῦ (ek sou, "out of you"). Her alone is named as the human source. "Therefore" is διό (dio, "for which reason"). The title "Son of God" is tied to this conception.

**[L4]** Matthew 1:18 and 1:20 name the Holy Ghost as the origin ([L1] with [L2] ek). Luke 1:35 names Mary as the only human source ([L3] with [L2] ek sou). Together they leave no place for a human begetter.

## III. Mary was a virgin, and no man had known her

**[L1] Luke 1:34:** "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"

**[L2]** "Know" is γινώσκω (ginōskō), used here as the Hebrew idiom for marital knowledge. "A man" is ἄνδρα (andra, "a male person, a husband"). Mary affirms that she has had no such relation with any man.

**[L3] Matthew 1:25:** "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son: and he called his name JESUS."

**[L3] Luke 1:27:** "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph…"

**[L2]** The word behind "virgin" in Luke 1:27 and Matthew 1:23 is παρθένος (parthenos, "virgin"). The same Greek ginōskō ("know") appears in Matthew 1:25 for Joseph. He did not know her until she had brought forth.

**[L3] Isaiah 7:14:** "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel."

**[L3] Matthew 1:23:** "Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel, which being interpreted is, God with us."

**[L2]** The Hebrew word standing behind the KJV's "virgin" in Isaiah 7:14 is הָעַלְמָה (ha-ʿalmāh, H5959). Matthew 1:23 quotes the verse and renders it with parthenos.

**[L4]** The conception is placed before Joseph and Mary "came together" (Matthew 1:18 [L1]). Mary denies knowing any man (Luke 1:34 [L1], with [L2] ginōskō). Matthew 1:23 applies Isaiah 7:14 to this birth ([L3]). So no human male took part in the conception.

**[L1] Hebrews 10:5:** "…a body hast thou prepared me."

**[L2]** The word for "body" is σῶμα (sōma, "body"). It is said to be "prepared", not begotten by a man.

# Opening: Christ had no biological father

**Terms.** By "biological father" I mean a male parent who begat the child through natural generation. I hold that Christ had none. His mother was a virgin, and the child was conceived by the Holy Ghost, not by Joseph or any man. [L4, resting on the verses below]

## 1. Matthew's genealogy breaks its own pattern at Joseph

[L1] Matthew 1:2: "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob; and Jacob begat Judas and his brethren". [L1] Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."

[L2] The verb in the chain is *gennaō* (G1080, "to beget"), active, with a male subject each time. At Jesus it changes to the passive *egennēthē* ("was born"). The relative pronoun *hēs* ("of whom") is feminine singular, so it points to Mary alone. It is not "of whom" in the plural, and it is not "begat Jesus".

[L3] Matthew 1:16 calls Joseph "the husband of Mary", not the one who begat. The same chapter says in Matthew 1:18 that Mary was "espoused to Joseph, before they came together".

[L4] The footing is the active "begat" (Matthew 1:2) against the passive "was born" with a feminine "of whom" (Matthew 1:16, *gennaō*). Together they show that the line of begetting stops at Joseph and the child's origin is traced to Mary only.

## 2. The conception is ascribed to the Holy Ghost

[L1] Matthew 1:18: "she was found with child of the Holy Ghost." [L2] *ek pneumatos hagiou* means "out of [the] Holy Spirit". *Ek* (G1537) marks source or origin.

[L1] Matthew 1:20: "Joseph thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." [L2] *gennēthen* is the same root, *gennaō* (G1080), in the passive. The angel uses the verb of generation and names the Holy Ghost as its source (*ek*).

[L1] Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God." [L2] *episkiazō* (G1982, "to overshadow") is the verb of divine power. [L3] The "therefore" (*dio*) ties the child's identity as Son of God to this act.

[L4] Matthew 1:18 and 1:20 name the source (*ek*) of the conception as the Holy Ghost, and Luke 1:35 gives the mechanism, "come upon" and "overshadow". Two verses name the source and a third names the means, so no natural male source is left in the account.

## 3. Mary was a virgin and Joseph "knew her not"

[L1] Luke 1:27: "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph". [L2] *parthenos* (G3933) means virgin. [L1] Luke 1:34: "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?" [L2] *andra ou ginōskō* ("a man I know not") uses *ginōskō* (G1097), "to know", in the sense of marital intimacy.

[L1] Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son". [L2] The same verb, *eginōsken*, is negated up to the birth.

## 4. Verses calling Joseph "father" are answered by the text itself

Precept upon precept, the rows interlock and none is set against another.

So the record holds at [L4], footed on these rows: Christ had a biological father. Joseph, of the house and lineage of David, is the named father, and the child is "made of the seed of David according to the flesh" (Romans 1:3).
